title: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: MOM workforce reforms
sections.summary: The motion seeks a $100 reduction in Head S, citing MOM reforms including COMPASS and the Platform Workers Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head S of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Over the current term of Government, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has undertaken bold reforms to steer our workforce from crisis to recovery, from downturn to growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We introduced the Complementarity Assessment (COMPASS) framework to ensure foreign talent complements and never displaces our Singaporean core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We legislated the world's first Platform Workers Act to protect more than 70,000 workers who have been under-protected for too long.

sections.label: Ageing workforce and support ratio
sections.summary: Seniors' workforce share rose to 16.9% in 2024, the old-age support ratio worsened to 3.5:1, and senior participation is 72.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The proportion of seniors in our workforce has risen from 12.3% in 2014 to 16.9% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Our old-age support ratio has worsened from 6:1 in 2014 to 3.5:1 today; and by 2030, it will drop to 2.7:1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Senior workforce participation in Singapore stands at 72.6%, trailing behind cities like Stockholm and Tokyo.

sections.label: Female labour force and pay gap
sections.summary: Female share of the resident labour force rose to 47.6%, and the adjusted gender pay gap narrowed to 6% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The share of females in the resident labour force has increased to 47.6% over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In 2023, the adjusted gender pay gap in Singapore narrowed to 6%.

sections.label: Women on boards target
sections.summary: Women on boards of top 100 SGX-listed firms reached 25.1% by December 2024, surpassing the 25% interim target for 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The proportion of women on boards for the top 100 Singapore Exchange-listed firms reached 25.1% by December 2024, surpassing the interim target of 25% set for 2025 by the Council for Board Diversity.

sections.label: Female representation in leadership
sections.summary: DBS has 40% women in senior management, but only 9% of Singaporean companies had female CEOs in 2024, below ASEAN's 21%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One good example is DBS Bank, where women constitute 40% of senior management, nearly double the 2021 industry average of 24.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, in Singapore, at the CEO level, only 9% of Singaporean companies have female CEOs as of 2024, lagging behind even our Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) peers, who clock in at 21%.

sections.label: Gender parity timeline
sections.summary: At current growth rates, gender parity in senior management will not materialise before the 2050s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: At current growth rates, gender parity in senior management will not materialise before 2050s.

sections.label: Improving HR standards and support
sections.summary: Proposes mandating IHRP certification, supporting HR continuing education and networks, and helping firms, especially SMEs, build human capital capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: One is to further improve our HR standards nationally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This can be done through mandating certification such as the Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP) certification as well as a mutual recognition of this certification with internationally recognised HR certifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Two, we can better support the HR profession by providing greater opportunities for continuing education and training (CET), professional network and development to create and catalyse progression possibilities for the profession to take on bigger roles in their organsations and industry locally and globally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The third is to support firms and businesses, especially small and medium enterprises (SMEs), to build their human capital function and capabilities, especially since the person managing HR may well be the administrative or finance person.

sections.label: Companies benefiting from job redesign grant
sections.summary: Asks how many companies have benefited from job redesign support under the Productivity Solutions Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How many companies have actually benefited from job redesign support under the Productivity Solutions Grant?

sections.label: Urging rebalance of manpower policy
sections.summary: States that over this term of Parliament he has constantly urged the Government to rebalance its manpower policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, over this term of Parliament, I have constantly urged this Government to rebalance its manpower policy, because we have heard from many Singaporeans that they are facing great difficulties in finding good jobs and holding on to those jobs.

sections.label: Employment statistics definition misuse
sections.summary: States that statistics can be misused because a worker counts as employed if he has worked only one hour per week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Statistics can also be misused to paint a wrong narrative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is because under the definition of our employment statistics, a worker is considered employed even if he has worked for only one hour per week.

sections.label: PMETs share of employed residents
sections.summary: Says the Minister stated last month that PMETs now make up 64% of all employed residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last month, the Minister said that professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) now make up 64% of all employed residents, which matches the proportion of residents with tertiary education in the workforce.

sections.label: Collecting data on prior residency status
sections.summary: Urges the Government to collect data on changes in resident employment and the resident labour force based on workers' prior residency status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Most recently, when I asked the Minister in May 2024 what percentage of the increase in resident employment by 4,900 in 2023 is due to non-residents becoming residents in Singapore, the Minister replied, "This line of questioning is not productive and undermines social cohesion in Singapore." He also added that MOM does not collect data on the net change in resident employment by workers' prior residency status in its labour market survey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, without tracking the resident labour force based on the workers' prior residency status, I wonder how the Minister can conclude that there is no significant underemployment in Singapore and that I am looking for a smoking gun.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to start collecting data on changes in resident employment and the resident labour force based on the worker's prior residency status.

sections.label: 1979 graduate starting salary
sections.summary: In 1979, the median starting salary of a university graduate was $957 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 1979, the median starting salary of a university graduate was $957 per month.

sections.label: HDB flat prices versus salaries
sections.summary: It compares 1979 and 2024 HDB flat prices with median starting salaries of university and VITB graduates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In July 1979, after a 15% price increase by the Housing and Development Board (HDB), the price of a new 4-room flat sold by the HDB in new towns was $27,100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is equivalent to about 28 times the median starting salary of a university graduate, or 43 times the median starting salary of a VITB graduate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Today, the median starting salary of a university graduate is $4,500 per month as of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the October 2024 Built-To-Order (BTO) launch exercise, the cheapest 4-room flats launched, excluding grants, cost $290,000, or 64 times the median starting salary of a university graduate, while the cheapest 5-room flats cost $427,000, or 95 times the median graduate starting salary.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit rollout timing
sections.summary: A speaker asks if MOM can accelerate the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit rollout, scheduled for end-2026, citing urgency of job redesign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The recent revamp of the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit is a welcome move, but its rollout is only scheduled for end-2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Given the urgency of job redesign, can the MOM consider accelerating its implementation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A delayed rollout could result in businesses deferring critical transformation projects while they wait for funding.

sections.label: Southeast Asia HR certification scheme
sections.summary: Singapore is believed to be the only country in Southeast Asia with an HR certification scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore is believed to be the only country in Southeast Asia with an HR certification scheme.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model and productivity
sections.summary: Wage growth must be driven by productivity gains and not just Government support, while the Progressive Wage Model is a step forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) is a great step forward, wage growth must be driven by productivity gains and not just Government support.

sections.label: Employers' concerns over Shared Parental Leave
sections.summary: Many employers expressed concerns over the impact on their manpower when the additional 10 weeks of Shared Parental Leave was announced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, many employers expressed concerns over the impact on their manpower when the additional 10 weeks of Shared Parental Leave was announced.

sections.label: Parental leave and foreign manpower quota
sections.summary: Suggests re-allocating foreign manpower quota to employers with desired HR practices, such as welcoming parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, if employers know that an employee taking 30 days of parental leave would allow them to have access to an additional foreign personnel for 60 weeks, would this not make them more welcoming of their employees taking parental leave?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At the national level, we can continue to limit the supply of foreign manpower coming into Singapore, but re-allocate the quota towards employers with desired HR practices from other employers.

sections.label: Rewarding family-friendly leave
sections.summary: Companies offering family-friendly leave beyond statutory requirements should be rewarded further.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Companies that offer additional family-friendly leave on top of statutory requirements should be rewarded further.

sections.label: Workforce outcomes for Government grants
sections.summary: Asks whether MOM would work with economic agencies to guide grant-seeking companies to commit to workforce outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To reinforce workforce transformation alongside business transformation, would MOM work with economic agencies to guide companies seeking Government grants to also commit to workforce outcomes such as job redesign to raise job worth, training for lower-skilled workforce and programmes to develop Singaporean talent?

sections.label: Workforce Transformation Map effectiveness
sections.summary: Asks how effective the Workforce Transformation Map has been and how success of support schemes is measured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How effective has the Workforce Transformation Map been in guiding companies and how do we measure the success of these support schemes?

sections.label: AI impact on job redesign
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry is addressing AI's impact on job redesign and what support affected employees receive.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this context, how is the Ministry addressing the impact of AI on job redesign and what support is the Ministry providing to employees affected by AI and job redesign?

sections.label: Skills-based career development strategies
sections.summary: Asks what strategies promote skills-based career development and encourage employers to recognise and reward skills.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this context, what strategies are in place to promote skills-based career development, and to encourage employers to recognise and reward skills and competency?

sections.label: Career coaching job matching KPIs
sections.summary: Asks what KPIs ensure career coaching and job matching lead to actual hires, and the results, noting Budget 2025 gave localised job matching to CDCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What key performance indicators (KPIs) are in place to ensure that career coaching and job matching services lead to actual hires, and what are the results?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Budget 2025 Statement announced that localised job matching will now be done by Community Development Councils (CDCs).

sections.label: PME support measures update
sections.summary: Asks MOM for an update on past-decade PME measures and whether desired outcomes were achieved, and welcomes the Workplace Fairness Act and Jobseeker Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Mr Patrick Tay, take your two cuts together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: There have been a series of measures the past decade such as the Fair Consideration Framework, a National Jobs Bank called the MyCareersFuture portal as well as the formation of Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) and Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) to look into better supporting PMEs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I hope MOM can provide an update on all these schemes that have been rolled out and whether we have achieved the desired outcomes of these policies, programmes and penal and punitive actions on egregious employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I support and applaud the passing of the Workplace Fairness Act which will go some way when implemented to eradicate discriminatory practices in the workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I also welcome the introduction of the Jobseeker Support Scheme, something I have lobbied in and outside of this House for more than a decade.

sections.label: PME job placements doubled
sections.summary: PME job placements doubled from 8,800 in 2023 to 17,000 in 2024, described as a strong sign of momentum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: PME job placements doubled from 8,800 in 2023 to 17,000 in 2024 – a strong sign of momentum.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up top-up limits
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme's $4,000 top-up supports mid-career upskilling, but financial aid alone is not enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme's $4,000 top-up supports mid-career upskilling, but financial aid alone is not enough.

sections.label: Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme call
sections.summary: Calls for urgent implementation of the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme, first accepted by the Government in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I have been going on like a broken record, I hope we can urgently implement the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme, which was first accepted by the Government back in 2016.

sections.label: TAFEP complaint figures
sections.summary: Between 2014 and 2021, TAFEP received an average of 379 complaints a year, only a third warranted additional investigations, and 41 were found in breach.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Between 2014 and 2021, the TAFEP received an average of 379 complaints a year, but only a third warranted additional investigations and a mere 41 were found in breach of guidelines.

sections.label: Foreign talent cheaper without CPF
sections.summary: Existing local hiring solutions target symptoms, while foreign talents are often cheaper because they lack CPF.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Existing solutions to spur local hiring appear to be targeting only symptoms.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But the reason favouring the hiring of a foreign talent is that simply, without CPF, foreign talents are often just cheaper.

sections.label: CPF for foreigners via escrow
sections.summary: Enfolding foreigners into CPF could be a logistical and financial nightmare, so CPF-equivalent payouts could be held in escrow accounts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Enfolding foreigners into CPF could easily turn into an unnecessary logistical and financial nightmare.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We can set aside the CPF-equivalent payouts into individual specific accounts under an escrow, which will be returned to the foreign worker once they depart.

sections.label: Foreign worker schemes and dependency ratio
sections.summary: Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have similar schemes, and MOM's November 2024 report shows residents' dependency ratio fell from 6.0 in 2014 to 3.5 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Other jurisdictions with large foreign worker populations, such as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, already have schemes in place that are similar.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Chairman, MOM's November 2024 report highlights a decline in Singapore's residents' dependency ratio from 6.0 in 2014 to 3.5 in 2024, underscoring the growing financial strain on our workforce, especially in our senior care.

sections.label: Cross-deployment and composite DRC
sections.summary: The AfA on Business Competitiveness recommended expanding cross-deployment of foreign workers beyond sectoral boundaries and asked about a composite Dependency Ratio Ceiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The AfA on Business Competitiveness has recommended expanding cross-deployment of foreign workers beyond sectoral boundaries to help businesses optimise manpower amid demand fluctuations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, how feasible would it be to introduce a composite Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) for companies expanding into adjacent industries with transferable skillsets, allowing them to scale without being constrained by sector-specific foreign worker quotas?

sections.label: Work Permit changes and COMPASS impact
sections.summary: Planned Work Permit changes aim to alleviate sector-specific labour shortages, and MOM was asked about COMPASS's early impact on skilled labour recruitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Additionally, planned changes to Work Permit policies, such as the expansion of the Non-Traditional Sources Occupation List and Non-Traditional Source countries, along with the relaxed Work Permit requirements, aim to alleviate sector-specific labour shortages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In this context, could MOM provide insights into the early impact of COMPASS on skilled labour recruitment?

sections.label: 1968 holiday reduction decision
sections.summary: MOM said a 1968 decision reduced holidays to stay competitive, so Muslims gave up the Prophet Muhammad's birthday, Christians Easter Monday, and Hindus chose Deepavali over Thaipusam.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim:
sentences.text: The response from MOM was that it was the result of a decision made in 1968 to reduce the number of holidays to stay competitive.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim:
sentences.text: As a result, Muslims gave up the Prophet Muhammad's birthday, Christians relinquished Easter Monday, while Hindus chose Deepavali over Thaipusam.

sections.label: Indian community holiday count
sections.summary: Easter weekend included Friday and Monday alongside Christmas, so the Indian community had a smaller number of holidays to begin with.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim:
sentences.text: Easter weekend included Friday and Monday, alongside Christmas.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim:
sentences.text: Hence, when called to give up a holiday, the Indian community had to do so with a smaller number to begin with.

sections.label: Thaipusam holiday reinstatement call
sections.summary: A 1968 promise by EW Barker to restore holidays if Singapore prospered is invoked to reinstate Thaipusam and review seven days of annual leave.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim:
sentences.text: In the debate surrounding the Holidays (Amendment) Bill in 1968, which rescinded Thaipusam as a holiday, then-Minister for Law and Economic Development EW Barker, went as far as to suggest, "If our island prospers, I am sure the Government will ask me to come back here and, on that day, it will be my pleasure to move amendments to increase the number of holidays." Between 1968 and today, our gross domestic product (GDP) per capita has grown from a little more than $2,100 to more than $127,000 – close to a sixtyfold increase.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim:
sentences.text: It is impossible to claim that we have not prospered.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim:
sentences.text: It is time to call in that promise made close to six decades ago and reinstate Thaipusam as a national holiday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It has been 57 years since we reviewed our minimum entitlement of only seven days of annual leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is time to review this to help all workers, especially the 18,800 employees who receive only seven days of annual leave.

sections.label: Kickback penalties increase
sections.summary: Laws need more deterrent effect, so the maximum sentence should rise to five years' imprisonment and a $100,000 fine, matching bribery penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need our laws to have a more deterrent effect to have any chance of wiping out kickbacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We should increase the maximum sentence to five years of imprisonment and a fine of $100,000, matching the maximum penalty for bribery cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

sections.label: Retrenchment guidelines for diversified workforce
sections.summary: MOM is asked whether it will update Tripartite Guidelines on retrenchment so M&A businesses can fairly manage lay-offs affecting emerging workforce groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
sentences.text: Given today's diversified workforce, does MOM plan to update the Tripartite Guidelines on Managing Excess Manpower and Responsible Retrenchment so that businesses planning for mergers and acquisitions (M&As) can apply differentiated yet fair approaches to manage lay-offs or contract cessations that affect emerging workforce, such as persons with disabilities, agency workers, freelancers and migrant workers?

sections.label: Employment Act review and AI workgroup
sections.summary: MOM is asked to set up an AI workgroup and review the Employment Act, raising salary caps and clarifying section 18A on transfers.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
sentences.text: Could MOM share if it would set up an inter-governmental workgroup to guide fair use of AI in the context of workforce rights and responsibilities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: With the rise in median wages, changes in the nature of work, workforce and workplaces, I am asking MOM to embark on a review of the Employment Act with our tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: First, is in relation to Part IV of the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I submit that both the salary caps as stipulated in section 35 of $2,600 and $4,500 respectively be raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Second, there continues to be questions in the interpretation of section 18A of the Employment Act on transfers which impact workers affected by ongoing company restructuring, M&As.

sections.label: Reasons for employer termination
sections.summary: Employers currently terminate with notice pay but no reasons, and the question asks if they can be made to give reasons explicitly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: At present, I am aware that employers terminate employees with notice pay but without giving reasons for the termination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Can employers be made to give their reasons for termination or discontinuation of employment explicitly in all cases of cessation of employment initiated by the employer?

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package
sections.summary: The SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package assisted over 200,000 jobseekers, with resident unemployment now at 2.8%, among the lowest compared to OECD countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, we assisted more than 200,000 jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Now, resident unemployment is at 2.8%, amongst the lowest compared to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries.

sections.label: Median real monthly income growth
sections.summary: Over five years, median real monthly income of residents grew 3.6%, and for lower-wage workers it was higher at 5.9%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Over the last five years, the median real monthly income of residents grew by 3.6%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For lower-wage workers, this was even higher at 5.9%.

sections.label: Retirement adequacy and Majulah Package
sections.summary: Retirement adequacy was strengthened with the $9 billion Majulah Package in 2024 and over $800 million for the enhanced Silver Support Scheme for 290,000 seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We strengthened the retirement adequacy of all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We introduced the $9 billion Majulah Package in 2024 and we expect to spend over $800 million on the enhanced Silver Support Scheme this year for 290,000 seniors.

sections.label: Working-age residents supporting elderly
sections.summary: In 2014, six working-age residents supported each elderly resident aged 65 and above; in 2024 this fell to 3.5.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In 2014, there were six working-age residents supporting each elderly resident aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In 2024, last year, this fell to 3.5.

sections.label: Labour productivity growth with ITMs
sections.summary: Supported by the Industry Transformation Maps, labour productivity grew by around 2% per annum over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Supported by the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), labour productivity grew by around 2% per annum over the last decade.

sections.label: Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package
sections.summary: Companies need to transform their workforce with business improvements, and over $400 million will be set aside for a new Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To stay competitive, companies need to transform their workforce in tandem with business improvements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will set aside over $400 million for a new Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package.

sections.label: Workforce Development Grant increase
sections.summary: The Workforce Development Grant will be increased to 70%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Under the Workforce Development Grant, we will increase this to 70%.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup on HR capability
sections.summary: A Tripartite Workgroup on Human Capital Capability Development will be launched to raise HR standards and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: HR plays an important role in workforce transformation, not just to comply with employment legislation but also to uplift organisations' human capital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will launch a Tripartite Workgroup on Human Capital Capability Development to raise HR standards and HR professionals' capabilities to contribute strategically to business and workforce outcomes.

sections.label: EP and S Pass growth
sections.summary: Over the last decade, EP and S Pass holders grew by 38,000 while resident PMETs grew by 382,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: They probably have a deeper depth of knowledge and understanding of the trends than probably you and I do.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: So, over the last decade, the number of EP and S Pass holders grew by 38,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Resident PMETs grew by 382,000, 10 times more.

sections.label: ONE Passes issued in 2024
sections.summary: About 3,000 ONE Passes were issued in 2024, attracting global talent who create opportunities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The ONE Pass has continued to attract global talent who create opportunities in Singapore, and about 3,000 ONE Passes were issued in 2024.

sections.label: Minimum qualifying salary increase
sections.summary: The minimum qualifying salary was increased from $5,000 to $5,600 on 1 January 2025, with no further changes this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)

sections.summary: The PWM, LQS and Progressive Wage Mark accreditation scheme now benefit up to nine in 10 lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Our suite of Progressive Wage measures – the PWM, LQS and the Progressive Wage Mark accreditation scheme – now benefit up to nine in 10 lower-wage workers today.

sections.label: Real wage growth percentiles
sections.summary: From 2019 to 2024, real wages at the 20th percentile rose cumulatively by 5.9%, higher than the median worker at 3.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: From 2019 to 2024, real wages at the 20th percentile rose cumulatively by 5.9%, higher than the median worker at 3.6%.

sections.label: Security officers PWM markline
sections.summary: Security officers' minimum PWM markline is $2,870 today and will be $3,530 by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Today, it is $2,870 and, by 2028, our security officers will have a minimum PWM markline of $3,530.

sections.label: WIS qualifying income cap
sections.summary: From January 2025, the qualifying monthly income cap for WIS increased from $2,500 to $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: From January 2025, the qualifying monthly income cap for WIS has been increased from $2,500 to $3,000.

sections.label: WIS payments increase
sections.summary: In total, WIS payments will increase to $1.4 billion in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In fact, in total, WIS payments will increase to $1.4 billion in 2025.

sections.label: WSS Level-Up tier
sections.summary: WSS will be enhanced by introducing a new tier of support, WSS (Level-Up).

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As announced at Budget, we will enhance WSS by introducing a new tier of support in the form of WSS (Level-Up).

sections.label: WSS Level-Up trainee allowances
sections.summary: Full-time trainees get a monthly allowance of 50% of average monthly income, minimum $300, benefiting workers aged 30 and above earning up to $3,000 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Full-time trainees will receive a monthly allowance set at 50% of their average monthly income based on the latest available 12-month period, and this, with a minimum monthly allowance of $300.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This will benefit workers aged 30 and above, earning up to $3,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, effectively, WSS (Level-Up) trainees will receive up to $18,000 per year for full-time training and up to $3,600 per year for part-time training.

sections.label: PWCS co-funding increase
sections.summary: Government's co-funding of wage increases to low-wage workers rises from 30% to 40% in 2025 and 15% to 20% in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As outlined by the Prime Minister at Budget, we are enhancing the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS) support for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We will raise Government's co-funding of wage increases to low-wage workers from 30% to 40% in 2025 and from 15% to 20% in 2026.

sections.label: PWCS wage increases disbursed
sections.summary: The Government disbursed $2.7 billion of PWCS for 2022 and 2023 wage increases to over 520,000 employees by over 90,000 employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For wage increases given in 2022 and 2023, the Government has already disbursed $2.7 billion of PWCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: These co-funded wage increases were given to more than 520,000 employees by over 90,000 employers.

sections.label: Workplace fatality rate trends
sections.summary: The workplace fatality rate averaged 1.1 per 100,000 workers over five years, but recent 2024 fatalities require vigilance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Over the past five years, the workplace fatality rate has averaged at 1.1 per 100,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This places Singapore among the top performing countries, with just four OECD countries consistently performing below 1.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: However, the recent increase in workplace fatalities in the second half of 2024 underscores the need for all stakeholders to remain vigilant and to prioritise workplace safety.

sections.label: Video surveillance at construction worksites
sections.summary: Construction worksites with contract value of $5 million and above must install a Video Surveillance System.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Construction worksites with contract value of $5 million and above are required to install a Video Surveillance System (VSS).

sections.label: Total WSH Programme access
sections.summary: Under the Tripartite Oversight Committee on WSH, more than 136,000 workers have access to the Total WSH Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Under the Tripartite Oversight Committee on WSH, more than 136,000 workers have access to the Total WSH Programme.

sections.label: Tripartite advisory on reasonable accommodations
sections.summary: A tripartite advisory for reasonable accommodations is being developed to foster inclusive workplaces for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To foster inclusive workplaces for persons with disabilities, we are developing a tripartite advisory for reasonable accommodations.

sections.label: Enabling Employment Credit extended
sections.summary: About 630 persons with disabilities are placed into jobs yearly, and MOM will extend the Enabling Employment Credit until 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Each year, about 630 persons with disabilities are successfully placed into jobs through this programme, and more than 80% of them remain in employment for at least six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To further facilitate the employment of persons with disabilities, MOM will extend the Enabling Employment Credit (EEC), for three years, until 2028.

sections.label: MRSS expansion to disabled Singaporeans
sections.summary: The MRSS will be expanded to include eligible Singaporeans with disabilities of all ages from 1 January 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: As announced by the Prime Minister, the MRSS will be expanded to include eligible Singaporeans with disabilities of all ages from 1 January 2026.

sections.label: Uplifting Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: MOM will extend the Uplifting Employment Credit for three years, until 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Building on the positive responses, MOM will be extending the Uplifting Employment Credit for three years, until 2028.

sections.label: Employment rate for women
sections.summary: The employment rate for women aged 25 to 64 rose from 73.3% in 2019 to 78.3% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The employment rate for women aged 25 to 64 increased from 73.3% in 2019 to 78.3% in 2024.

sections.label: CCP enhancement for reskilling
sections.summary: From 1 April 2025, CCPs will be enhanced to support reskilling of mid-career new hires and employees in flexi-load jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: These roles span about 30 sectors, including financial services, retail, built environment, and information and communications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: However, from 1 April 2025 onwards, we will enhance CCPs to support reskilling of mid-career new hires and employees in jobs with flexi-load arrangements such as part-time work.

sections.label: WSG salary funding during training
sections.summary: During training, WSG will fund up to 90% of the worker's salary, capped at $7,500 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: During the training period, WSG will fund up to 90% of the worker's salary, capped at $7,500 per month.

sections.label: Firms offering flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: The proportion of firms offering FWAs increased from 68.1% in 2023 to 72.7% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: With a formal FWA policy in place, Sheng Siong is able to observe trends in their employees’ needs, which helps the company identify ways to support their employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the proportion of firms offering FWAs increased in the last year from 68.1% in 2023 to 72.7% in 2024.

sections.label: Women on boards, workplace fairness
sections.summary: Women on boards of top 100 SGX-listed companies reached 25.1% by end December 2024, and the Workplace Fairness Bill adds protection against workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Through the Council for Board Diversity’s efforts to shift mindsets of boards towards appointing more diverse candidates, as of end December 2024, the percentage of women on boards of top 100 Singapore Exchange-listed companies reached 25.1%, which is a more than three-fold increase from 7.5% in 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The Workplace Fairness Bill, which was passed earlier this year, will provide an additional layer of protection against workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To reiterate, the Government does not tolerate any form of workplace discrimination, including discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity.

sections.label: Employment credits for disabled, ex-offenders
sections.summary: MOM will extend the Enabling Employment Credit and Uplifting Employment Credit until 2028, with up to $400 monthly for hiring persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   To encourage employers to provide job opportunities for persons with disabilities and ex-offenders, MOM will extend both the Enabling Employment Credit and the Uplifting Employment Credit until 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Under the Enabling Employment Credit, eligible employers who hire persons with disabilities can receive up to $400 per month in employment credits.

sections.label: Matched Retirement Savings Scheme expansion
sections.summary: From 2026, the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme will be expanded to benefit eligible persons with disabilities regardless of their age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: From 2026, we will also expand the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme to benefit eligible persons with disabilities regardless of their age.

sections.label: S Pass qualifying salary benchmark
sections.summary: The S Pass qualifying salary is benchmarked to the top one third of local associate professionals and technicians' wages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our S Pass qualifying salary is benchmarked to the top one third of our local associate professionals and technicians' (APTs') wages.

sections.label: Moderated S Pass salary increase
sections.summary: The S Pass qualifying salary increase is moderated, applying to new applications from 1 September 2025 and renewals expiring from 1 September 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: MOM has taken into consideration and we have heard from various trade associations and chambers on the rising costs of manpower as well as their constraints in hiring.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Therefore, even though we have earlier announced this two years in advance and even though we are going ahead with the third step increase, what we have done this time round is to moderate the increase to give businesses more time to adjust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: So, the S Pass qualifying salary announced this year will only apply to new applications from 1 September this year, 2025, and renewal applications for passes expiring from next year, 1 September 2026.

sections.label: Work Permit maximum employment age
sections.summary: After SME feedback, the maximum employment age for Work Permit holders was raised, letting firms retain experienced workers despite potentially higher insurance costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It is the collective feedback, working with all the different small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) on the ground, the general consensus is that once the workers have been here for quite some time, the skillsets, the experience that they have already gained, it would be a waste for them, after they reached a certain period or ceiling of maximum employment period, to leave the country.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: So, what we did after taking their feedback into their consideration, we raised the maximum employment age for Work Permit holders so that we can give these firms the flexibility to retain their more experienced, more skilled workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Firms have the option and they are best placed for themselves to assess the benefits of retaining their more experienced workers against the potentially higher insurance costs that they may have to bear for these older workers.

sections.label: Job Support scheme extension
sections.summary: The JS scheme was extended to Cambodia, Laos and Bhutan, and applies to retrenched employees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For a start, we extended it to Cambodia, Laos and Bhutan, because these are the countries that we do have very strong networks and also bilateral diplomatic ties with.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To be clear, the JS scheme is aimed to cushion unemployment shocks as a result of economic transformation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, it applies to employees, who have no control over the decision by their employers to retrench them.

sections.label: Qualifying salary and involuntary unemployment
sections.summary: The speaker says proving involuntary unemployment is hard and would only work when wages fall below S Pass or EP thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think it is very hard for us to prove a priori whether that kind of issue constitutes involuntary unemployment, which is quite different from an employee.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But respectfully, I believe that this would only work in a special case when wages for a given position are lower than the S Pass or EP threshold, which is currently set at $3,300 and $5,600 a month, although this adjusts upward with age and for rehires.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Lim, do you want to get to your clarification?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: So, the question is, if the Minister could explain how the qualifying salary in such instances would address this situation?

sections.label: EP, S Pass and PMET numbers
sections.summary: From 2014 to 2024 EP and S Pass holders rose 38,000 while resident PMET jobs rose 382,000, with low citizen unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: At those levels, what we have seen consistently – and this is real, the numbers, the statistics do not lie – over the last 10 years, I have stated, notwithstanding the fact that we have this qualifying salary, from 2014 to 2024, the number of EP and S Pass holders increased by 38,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But over that same corresponding period, the number of residents holding PMET jobs increased by 382,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the record, in June 2024, the unemployment rate for Singapore Citizens was 2.8%, which is amongst the lowest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If you look at our long-term unemployment, it is around about 0.7%, 0.8%.

sections.label: Gender pay gap question
sections.summary: The passage asks what Singapore's current gender pay gap is and how the Government plans to reduce it further.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: What is the current gender pay gap in Singapore and how does the Government plan to reduce it further?

sections.label: Gender pay gap figures
sections.summary: Singapore's unadjusted gender pay gap fell from 16.0% in 2002 to 14.3% in 2023, and the adjusted gap from 8.8% to 6.0%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Singapore's unadjusted gender pay gap has reduced from 16.0% in 2002 to 14.3% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Our adjusted gender pay gap, which adjusts for differences in occupation, industry, hours worked, age and education, narrowed from 8.8% in 2002 to 6.0% in 2023.

sections.label: Women in STEM jobs
sections.summary: Men still outnumber women in STEM occupations, though women's share rose from 28.8% in 2013 to 35.2% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Likewise, for STEM-related occupations, there is still a higher proportion of men than women although the proportion of women in STEM jobs has increased over time from 28.8% in 2013 to 35.2% in 2024.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Legislation gender pay gap
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness Legislation will help reduce the gender pay gap by protecting women from sex-based discrimination in careers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The Workplace Fairness Legislation will also help further reduce the gender pay gap, as women will be protected against discrimination based on their sex that could inhibit their entry into and progress in careers of their choice, especially in the male-dominated and higher-paying occupations.

sections.label: Local-born Citizens PMET increase
sections.summary: More than 63% of the increase in PMETs from 2014 to 2024 is due to local-born Singapore Citizens.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Since the Member persistently wants to keep harping on the division between foreign-born Singapore Citizens versus local-born Singapore Citizens, I just eyeballed the numbers, and I am happy to see what other statistics we can glean moving forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But the majority, more than 63% of the increase over that period for the PMETs from 2014 to 2024 – more than 63% of that increase – is due to local-born Singapore Citizens.

sections.label: University and polytechnic cohort shares
sections.summary: In 1979, 4% of each cohort went to university; today around 60% go to polytechnic and ITE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In 1979, only 4% of each cohort went to university.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Today, around 60% of each cohort go to polytechnic and the Institute of Technical Education (ITE).

sections.label: BTO and resale mortgage cash
sections.summary: Over eight in 10 first-timer households who collected keys in 2024 used little to no cash for HDB mortgage instalments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In fact, more than eight in 10 first-timer households who collected their keys to their Build-To-Order (BTO) flats and resale flats in 2024, used little to no cash to service their HDB monthly mortgage instalments.

sections.label: Construction boom and HDB prices
sections.summary: Around 1979/1980, construction costs rose 30% due to a boom, and HDB flat prices rose 15%, 20% and 38%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Around 1979/1980, construction cost went up by 30%, because there was a construction boom which led to severe labour and material shortages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, HDB flat prices went up by 15% in 1979, another 20% in 1980 and another 38% in 1981.

sections.label: Social compact and public housing
sections.summary: Singapore's social compact involves affordable housing giving Singaporeans a stake, and policies will remain relevant, affordable, accessible and inclusive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have developed our strong social compact where Singaporeans buy affordable housing, have a tangible stake in this country and form strong communities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: They want to go backwards to the time where housing was a shelter, an expense, and does not serve as a store of value and assurance for retirement, where Singaporeans do not have a stake when they leave, according to the AHS, just return keys, get some deposit back and move on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have come a long way since 1979.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will continue to look forward instead to ensure that our policies remain relevant, effective in providing public housing that is affordable, accessible and inclusive for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Minister Tan, a short one, because we are almost reaching our guillotine time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I wanted to reassure everyone, our economy grew significantly in the last decade.

sections.label: Equal upskilling opportunities for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government cannot guarantee the same outcomes for all Singaporeans but will do its best to give them the same opportunities to upskill, train and upgrade at every stage of their lives and careers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I think that was the gist of it already, I have translated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I want to reassure: while we may not be able to guarantee the same outcomes for all Singaporeans, but we will certainly do our level best that Singaporeans, at every stage of their lives, at every stage of their careers will have the same opportunities to upskill, to train and to upgrade.

sections.label: Thanks to ministers and MOM officers
sections.summary: The speaker thanks Minister Tan See Leng, Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon, Senior Minister of State Zaqy, Minister of State Gan Siow Huang, Permanent Secretaries Ng Chee Khern and Jeffrey Siow and MOM officers, and seeks leave to withdraw his amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to thank Minister Tan See Leng, Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon, Senior Minister of State Zaqy and Minister of State Gan Siow Huang for their comprehensive responses and driving policy changes; and also Permanent Secretaries Ng Chee Khern, Jeffrey Siow, and their team of MOM officers, for their dedication in building a great workforce and workplace for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: On that note, Chairman, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.
